title: Throat culture
what: A swab is taken from your throat. The lab grows the sample to see which germs live there and which medicines work on them.
why: For frequent tonsillitis, a sore throat that lasts, before a health resort stay or a job, or to check for staph carriage.
duration: the swab takes a few seconds; results usually come in 3 to 7 days
tell_doctor: If you take or recently took antibiotics
If you use throat sprays or gargles
If you have a strong gag reflex

prepare.title: Food and drink
prepare.text: The swab is usually taken before eating, or 2 to 3 hours after eating and drinking. Check with the clinic.

prepare.title: Throat and teeth
prepare.text: In the morning, do not gargle or use sprays. Brushing teeth is usually not advised. Check with the lab.

prepare.title: Antibiotics
prepare.text: The culture is best done before you start antibiotics. If you already take them, tell your doctor. Do not stop them on your own.

steps: You sit and open your mouth
Your tongue is held down with a flat stick
A sterile swab is rubbed over the tonsils and the back of the throat
The swab goes into a tube with a special gel
If a nose swab is also ordered, it is taken with a separate swab
feel: You may gag for a second
after: You can eat and drink right away
Results usually come in 3 to 7 days
The report may list which antibiotics work. Your doctor will go over it

faq.q: If staph is found, does that mean I am ill?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Many people carry it without harm. Your doctor decides if treatment is needed based on your symptoms.

faq.q: Why does a culture take so long?
faq.a: Germs need time to grow. Then they are tested against medicines.

reminders.text: Throat swab tomorrow. In the morning, do not eat, drink, or gargle, unless the clinic said otherwise.
